SEC.title: Pin all three stdio MCP servers — every session start executes unpinned upstream code with broad filesystem access

evidence.what: filesystem MCP launched via `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` with no version pin — this is the pre-existing MED already reported by /security-scan THIS session (cited, not re-derived). Its args grant access to the repo, the entire Bannerlord Modules dir, and E:\LOTRAOMAssets.
serena MCP launched via `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena` with no tag/rev pin — pulls and executes upstream git HEAD, with `--project` pointed at the TAOM repo.
git MCP launched via `uvx mcp-server-git` with no version pin — latest PyPI release executed each session, with full git access to the repo.

SEC.impact: A compromised or malicious release of any of these three upstream packages executes arbitrary code on the dev machine at every Claude session start, with read/write access to the repo, the game install, and asset drives. The /security-scan MED covered only the filesystem server; serena (git HEAD — no release gating at all) and mcp-server-git are the same class and were not flagged.
SEC.riskWhy: Pinning versions can only break MCP startup if the pinned version is wrong — immediately visible, trivially reverted; no game or save impact.
SEC.fixSketch: Pin filesystem to `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@<version>`, serena to a specific git rev/tag (`git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@<sha>`), and mcp-server-git to `mcp-server-git==<version>`. Add a bump cadence note to docs/migration/dr3-maintenance.md or the security-scan checklist so pins don't rot silently.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: As cited, with trivial block-end adjustments: serena block is .mcp.json lines 3-17 (cited 3-16), filesystem lines 22-33 (cited 22-31), git lines 34-39 (cited 34-38). All three claims verified against the file: serena = `uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena` (no tag/rev), filesystem = `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` (no @version) with args granting the repo + entire Bannerlord Modules dir + E:\LOTRAOMAssets, git = `uvx mcp-server-git` (no version). All three are active: enabled in .claude/settings.local.json lines 54-61 (`enabledMcpjsonServers`).
_verdict.reasoning: REAL, not a false positive. (1) Not by-design: no ADR, rule, memory note, or doc records unpinned MCP servers as accepted. The opposite — TAOM's own audit tool (tools/audit_claude_config.py:249-252) flags `npx -y` without @version as a MED ("auto-install/typosquat risk"), and the project's established convention favors pinning (docs/migration/dr3-maintenance.md BUTR version-pinning policy; .claude/skills/improve/references/audit-playbook.md:36 flags unpinned third-party actions). The security-scan SKILL.md:44 calls the npx case "real-but-low risk" advisory — acknowledged, not waived. (2) Not duplicate-of-tracked: searched open GitHub issues for mcp/pin — #91, #246, #8, #92 are unrelated (#92's "pinning" is about harness-facts semantics, verified by reading its body). (3) The finding adds genuinely new scope beyond the pre-existing /security-scan MED: the audit tool's check matches only the literal string "npx" (line 249), so the two uvx-launched servers are invisible to it — serena is the worst of the three (executes upstream git HEAD with zero release gating, pointed at the TAOM repo) and mcp-server-git runs latest PyPI with full git access. The finding correctly self-identifies the filesystem MED as cited-not-re-derived. One minor overstatement: "executes unpinned upstream code at every session start" — npx/uvx cache resolved packages, so a fresh upstream pull happens on cache miss/refresh rather than literally every session; the supply-chain exposure class (any new upstream release/commit can be executed with broad FS + git access) is accurate. Effort S / risk LOW / fix sketch are sound; the suggested bump-cadence note also closes the tool gap (extend audit_claude_config.py to cover uvx, or document the pins in the security-scan checklist).

SEC.title: Harden the native signature scanner before authoring v1.4.5 patterns: no ambiguity detection, and a literal CC pattern byte silently becomes a wildcard

evidence.what: FindPattern returns the FIRST match across the entire module image (code + data sections, per SizeOfImage from GetModuleBase) with no second-match scan; an ambiguous pattern silently resolves to the wrong address.

ParsePattern stores wildcards as kWildcardSentinel = 0xCC in the same byte buffer as literal bytes — an authored pattern containing a literal `CC` byte (INT3 padding is common around function prologues) is indistinguishable from a wildcard and matches ANY byte (skip at line 97: `if (expected == kWildcardSentinel) continue;`).

Header explicitly delegates ambiguity resolution to manual pattern authoring ("ambiguity should be resolved by the pattern itself") and acknowledges scanning the whole module range — the safety property is a comment, not code.

All 7 target signatures are currently `<PATTERN_TBD>` stubs (intentional per the file's placeholder note), so the risk is latent today — but pattern authoring for v1.4.5 is the documented next step, and step 4 of the authoring workflow (lines 21-24) makes uniqueness a manual test the runtime never enforces. Consumers (HairClothHook.cpp:298-302, CoversHeadHook.cpp:128-130) feed the unverified first match straight into MH_CreateHook.

SEC.impact: When v1.4.5 patterns are authored, a pattern that is non-unique (or that contains a literal CC byte and thus matches far more sites than intended) hooks the wrong address in TaleWorlds.Native.dll — arbitrary memory corruption in the game process that manifests as untraceable crashes far from the hook. The manual uniqueness test in the authoring workflow is exactly the kind of behavioral-preservation step the CLAUDE.md C++ port discipline says gets skipped.
SEC.riskWhy: Fail-closed-on-ambiguity can only turn a would-be wrong-site hook into a logged no-op (hooks already degrade gracefully to inert); separating the wildcard mask from byte values is a contained parser change. No save impact.
SEC.fixSketch: In FindPattern, continue scanning after the first match and return 0 (log 'ambiguous pattern') if a second match exists. Replace the in-band 0xCC sentinel with a parallel bool mask array (or reject literal CC in ParsePattern with a clear error). Optionally constrain the scan to executable sections via the PE section table. Unit-test the parser host-side.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: As cited, with two refinements: (1) HairClothHook.cpp FindPattern calls are at lines 298-300 inside ResolveOne (lines 291-303) — cited range 298-302 is essentially correct; (2) add SignatureScanner.h:8-13 as evidence — the kWildcardSentinel comment rationalizes 0xCC only for the haystack side (a wildcard matching a real 0xCC byte in memory) and never addresses the pattern-authoring hazard that ParseHexByte("CC") produces a byte indistinguishable from the wildcard sentinel, confirming the parser hazard is undocumented. MH_CreateHook consumption confirmed at CoversHeadHook.cpp:162 and HairClothHook.cpp:364.
_verdict.reasoning: All four evidence items verified verbatim against current source. FindPattern (SignatureScanner.cpp:91-101) returns the first match across the full module image with no second-match scan; ParsePattern (lines 41-62) stores wildcards in-band as 0xCC so an authored literal CC byte silently becomes match-anything (skip at line 97); all 7 Signatures.h patterns are <PATTERN_TBD> stubs (lines 61/73/85/96/107/119/131) with uniqueness delegated to manual authoring step 4 (lines 21-24); consumers feed the unverified match straight into MH_CreateHook. False-positive checks all fail to refute: (a) the first-match behavior is documented (SignatureScanner.h:29-30, docs/features/native-skin-fixes.md:207-210) but as a described limitation, not a deliberated by-design decision — and the finding already frames this correctly ("the safety property is a comment, not code"); the literal-CC parser hazard is entirely undocumented (header lines 8-13 only cover the haystack side); (b) evidence attribution is accurate to within 2 lines; (c) not duplicate-of-tracked — issue #82 (NativeSkinFixes umbrella) has zero mention of scanner ambiguity/sentinel hardening, the feature doc's dedicated issue is still "TODO", and no scanner issue exists in the tracked set. Supporting context strengthens the finding: CLAUDE.md's native C++ port discipline and rca-native-skin-fixes-port-2026-05-26.md document this exact failure class (manual safety steps in vendored C++ skipped under audit-budget pressure) as a recurring TAOM pattern, and v1.4.5 pattern authoring is the documented next step (feature doc Status line), making the latent risk imminent. Effort S / fail-closed fix sketch (second-match scan returning 0, parallel bool mask or reject literal CC, optional .text-section constraint) is technically sound — hooks already degrade gracefully to inert no-ops on a 0 return, so detection only converts a would-be wrong-site hook into a logged skip.

SEC.title: process_faction_map.py templates file paths into Python source executed by subprocess — quote-in-path breaks into code execution

evidence.what: find_alpha_bbox builds a Python program as an f-string and runs it via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", f"""...read_png_rgba(r'{filepath}')..."""])` (interpolation at line 260) — a path containing a single quote terminates the raw-string literal and the remainder is executed as Python.
crop_png_to_bbox uses the same f-string-into-`python -c` subprocess pattern for the crop helper, interpolating input/output paths the same way.

SEC.impact: Defensive-maintenance issue in a local dev tool: paths derive from the --input CLI dir joined with hardcoded region ids, so today only the developer can trigger it — but any future reuse of these helpers against externally-named files (downloaded asset packs, user-submitted maps) inherits a code-execution-via-filename hazard, and even benign paths containing an apostrophe (common in Windows user dirs) break the tool today.
SEC.riskWhy: Passing the path via argv instead of string templating is behavior-preserving for all valid inputs; the embedded helper script reads sys.argv instead of a literal.
SEC.fixSketch: Make the embedded helper read paths from sys.argv: `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", SCRIPT, filepath])` with `path = sys.argv[1]` inside the script (same for crop's input/output paths and numeric bbox args). Two call sites, one shared constant script string.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: Evidence block 1 is as cited: c:/Users/mikew/source/repos/TAOM/tools/process_faction_map.py, find_alpha_bbox spans lines 150-273; the f-string subprocess starts at line 161 and the path interpolation `read_png_rgba(r'{filepath}')` is exactly at line 260. Evidence block 2 needs a line correction: the subprocess f-string in crop_png_to_bbox starts at lines 283-284 (cited "282-284" is the pattern start, fine), but the actual path interpolation is at line 383 — `crop_and_save(r'{input_path}', r'{output_path}', {x}, {y}, {w}, {h}, {max_width})` — not within 282-284. Same hazard, correct file/function, interpolation line is 383.
_verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on all three false-positive classes. (1) Not by-design: no ADR, .claude rule, CLAUDE.md note, or review doc blesses f-string-into-`python -c`; the only doc mentions of the script are a directory listing inside docs/reviews/codex-adversarial-bandit-management-2026-05-27.md and a one-line catalog entry in tools/README.md. (2) Evidence is substantively correct — verified by reading the file: both helpers build the child program as an f-string and pass interpolated paths inside raw-string literals (`r'{filepath}'` line 260; `r'{input_path}', r'{output_path}'` line 383), so a single quote in the path terminates the literal and the remainder of the path is parsed/executed as Python in the child process; a trailing backslash would also break the raw-string. Only correction: block 2's interpolation line is 383, not 282-284. (3) Not duplicate-of-tracked: none of the listed open issues touch this tool or this pattern. The impact framing is honest and accurate per main(): `filepath = Path(args.input) / f"region_{region_id}.png"` (lines 503-504) and outputs derive from `--output` (lines 572-573), so today only the developer's own CLI args reach the template — this is a robustness/defensive-maintenance finding, not an exploitable attack surface — but a benign apostrophe-containing path (e.g. a Windows dir like O'Brien) breaks the tool right now, and any future reuse against externally-named files inherits code-exec-via-filename. The grep confirms the pattern is confined to exactly these 2 sites in this one file, matching the finding's scope. The fix sketch (pass paths/bbox values via argv, `sys.argv` in the embedded script) is correct, behavior-preserving, and small. Keep as SEC-03 LOW-risk/S-effort with the line-383 correction.

SEC.title: Pin MCP server packages in .codex/config.toml (unpinned npx -y / uvx fetch-and-execute with full inherited env)

evidence.what: filesystem MCP server launched via `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` with no version pin, granted the TAOM repo, two game ModuleData dirs, and E:/Decompiled_Bannerlord as roots
git MCP server launched via `uvx mcp-server-git` — same unpinned fetch-latest-from-PyPI-and-execute pattern
`[shell_environment_policy] inherit = "all"` — child MCP processes receive the user's full environment (incl. any API keys)
the same npx -y unpinned filesystem-MCP pattern — already flagged as the pre-existing MED by /security-scan this session (cited, not re-derived)

SEC.impact: Every Codex session resolves and executes the latest published npm/PyPI package version with the user's full environment and filesystem-MCP write access to the repo and game ModuleData. A compromised or typosquat-replaced release runs arbitrary code on the dev machine. /security-scan's audited scope (.claude/, .mcp.json, settings*.json, CLAUDE.md) does not include .codex/config.toml, so this instance is currently invisible to the existing gate.
SEC.riskWhy: Pinning versions only risks running a stale server until someone bumps the pin; no behavior change otherwise.
SEC.fixSketch: Pin exact versions: `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem@<ver>` in both .codex/config.toml and .mcp.json, and `mcp-server-git==<ver>` for uvx. Optionally extend tools/audit_claude_config.py's scan scope to include .codex/config.toml so the existing /security-scan gate covers it.

_verdict.confidenceAdjustment: keep — HIGH. Core evidence is verbatim-correct; no by-design record, no tracking issue; the project's own security doc favors pinning.
_verdict.correctedEvidence: Items 1, 2, 4: as cited (item 4's filesystem block spans .mcp.json lines 22-33, unpinned package name on line 27; cited 24-26 covers the npx/-y lines). Item 3: lines 9-10 are real, but the claim "child MCP processes receive the user's full environment" is unverified — Codex's shell_environment_policy is documented for shell/exec subprocesses, and nothing in-repo proves it applies to MCP server spawns; treat as amplifying context, not load-bearing. ADD new evidence strengthening the finding: (a) tools/audit_claude_config.py iterates only .claude/**, settings*.json, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md (docstring lines 11-12; iter_files ~313-317) — .codex/ absent; (b) scan_mcp (lines 227-230) parses JSON only, so the fix requires tomllib support, not merely adding the path; (c) the mcp-npx-unpinned rule (lines 249-252) matches npx only — the uvx servers inside the audited .mcp.json itself (git → unpinned mcp-server-git, lines 34-39; serena → uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena tracking git HEAD, lines 3-17) are also invisible to the gate.
_verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed on all three false-positive classes. (1) By-design: .claude/skills/security-scan/SKILL.md:44 calibrates unpinned npx -y as a "real-but-low risk" advisory — an acknowledgment the risk class is real, not an acceptance/ADR; docs/ai-includes/security.md:283-292 ("Version Pinning") mandates exact pins and avoiding floating versions, so project policy supports the fix direction; no doc records .codex/config.toml's exclusion from the audit as deliberate (the tool is a 2026-05-29 AgentShield port whose scope simply never included .codex/). (2) Mis-attribution: only item 3's mechanism claim is overstated (shell_environment_policy → MCP child env is unproven from repo evidence); corrected, not rejected — the finding stands on items 1, 2, 4 alone. (3) Duplicate-of-tracked: open-issue list checked — all feature/bug items, none cover MCP pinning, .codex/config.toml, or audit scope. The finding adds genuinely new scope beyond the known .mcp.json MED: the same unpinned fetch-and-execute pattern in a file invisible to /security-scan, plus (verifier-added) the JSON-only parser and npx-only rule gaps that leave even .mcp.json's uvx servers unscanned. Fix sketch is sound with one nuance: extending the audit to .codex/config.toml requires TOML parsing (tomllib) and a uvx-aware rule, still EFFORT S.

SEC.title: Strip upstream GitHub Packages credential pair from local vendored UIExtenderEx nuget.config before it can ride a port into the public repo

evidence.what: <packageSourceCredentials> block for the nuget.pkg.github.com/BUTR feed containing a username plus an HTML-entity-encoded ClearTextPassword (GitHub personal access token shape). Value not reproduced per audit rules.
`Dependencies/.vendor-source/` is gitignored — confirmed via git check-ignore; the file is local-only, NOT committed (rg -uu sweep of the vendor tree found exactly this one instance)

SEC.impact: Currently zero exposure (untracked, repo public per gh repo view). The latent risk: .vendor-source is the /adopt-external staging ground for porting upstream code; copying this subtree (or un-ignoring it) would publish a third-party access token in a PUBLIC repo, and the HTML-entity encoding is precisely the form that evades GitHub push protection and secret scanning. Defensive-maintenance fix, not an active leak.
SEC.riskWhy: Deleting the credentials block from a gitignored reference copy breaks nothing — TAOM.sln does not build the vendor-source projects (grepped: no vendor-source project rows in the solution).
SEC.fixSketch: Delete the <packageSourceCredentials> block (or the whole nuget.config) from the local vendor copy. Add a `packageSourceCredentials|ClearTextPassword` grep to the /adopt-external security-vet checklist so future vendored drops are swept before any file is ported into the tracked tree. Rotation is upstream's (BUTR's) call — it is their token, shipped in their release source.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: as cited — nuget.config lines 8-13 and .gitignore line 112 both verified exactly. Supplementary verified detail: the ClearTextPassword decodes to a 40-hex-char legacy-format GitHub PAT (no ghp_ prefix), so it also evades TAOM's own docs/ai-includes/security.md pattern table; rg -uu confirms it is the only credential instance and only nuget.config in the vendor tree; repo visibility confirmed PUBLIC via gh repo view.
_verdict.reasoning: Every evidence claim reproduced first-hand: (1) the packageSourceCredentials block exists at the cited path/lines with HTML-entity-encoded username + ClearTextPassword (PAT shape, values not reproduced); (2) git check-ignore resolves to .gitignore:112 Dependencies/.vendor-source/, git ls-files shows 0 tracked vendor files, and git grep finds no committed ClearTextPassword/packageSourceCredentials anywhere — so zero current exposure, exactly as the finding states. Checked all three false-positive classes: NOT by-design (the .gitignore comment + dr3-mcm-internalization-plan explain why .vendor-source is ignored, but no doc/ADR/rule records the credential as known); NOT mis-attributed (file/lines exact); NOT duplicate-of-tracked (open-issue sweep matched only #8, an unrelated Harmony version mismatch; none of the known tracked issues are security items). The fix sketch is genuinely additive: /adopt-external SKILL.md has no credential-sweep step, external-repo-adoption.md step 2 covers code-that-reads-credentials (behavioral exfil) not committed credential files, and /security-scan scopes to .claude config, not Dependencies/. Two calibration notes that temper but do not refute: the token is BUTR's own, already published by upstream in their public release source (finding concedes this — rotation is theirs), so this is hygiene/latent-risk, not an active leak, exactly as the IMPACT honestly frames it; and because .vendor-source is re-downloaded fresh from GitHub tags each session per the .gitignore comment, the one-time local deletion is non-durable — the /adopt-external checklist grep is the load-bearing half of the fix. Finding is real, correctly scoped as S-effort defensive maintenance, HIGH confidence justified.

SEC.title: Enforce pattern-uniqueness and section-bounded scanning in SignatureScanner before the 1.4.5 patterns are authored

evidence.what: FindPattern scans the entire module image (base..SizeOfImage, headers + data + code) and returns the FIRST match with no uniqueness verification
the authoring procedure requires 'Test by checking the scan returns a single match' — but only as a manual step; the runtime never re-checks
all 7 signatures are currently <PATTERN_TBD> stubs (documented-inert state per docs/features/native-skin-fixes.md:249-253), so the gate can land before any live pattern exists

SEC.impact: When the 7 patterns are authored for v1.4.5 (or the next engine bump silently shifts code), an under-discriminating pattern that matches a wrong site first makes MinHook write a detour into arbitrary code or data — memory corruption / undefined crashes in the game process instead of the designed clean refusal-to-install. This is the playbook's 'byte-pattern scan matching the wrong site' class, and the only enforcement today is a comment.
SEC.riskWhy: The check runs once at install time; worst case a genuinely ambiguous pattern refuses to install and the hook stays inert with a clear log line — which is already the designed degraded mode.
SEC.fixSketch: After the first match, continue scanning for a second; if found, log both RVAs and return 0 (refuse install). Optionally walk the PE section headers and restrict the scan to executable sections. ~20 lines in SignatureScanner.cpp; no managed-side change.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: As cited, all four items verified. (1) SignatureScanner.cpp:88-101 — first-match return at line 100, no uniqueness re-check, no PE-section bounding; whole-image scope confirmed via GetModuleBase returning MODULEINFO.SizeOfImage (SignatureScanner.cpp:76) passed through by all three hooks (CoversHeadHook.cpp:121/128, HairClothHook.cpp:310/298, FaceMeshObserveHook.cpp:147-149). (2) Signatures.h:21-24 verbatim — single-match test is a manual authoring comment only. (3) Signatures.h:59-135 — all 7 TargetSignature constants are "<PATTERN_TBD>" with nullptr fallbacks. (4) docs/features/native-skin-fixes.md:249-254 confirms the documented-inert stub state. SUPPLEMENTARY evidence strengthening the finding: SignatureScanner.h:29-35 documents the first-match contract as relying on pattern authoring ("ambiguity should be resolved by the pattern itself") — i.e., the no-runtime-check behavior is known and comment-documented, not enforced; and HairClothHook.cpp:352-355 shows the four helper targets are cast to raw function pointers and CALLED DIRECTLY (kAddToList is mandatory, line 343) — a wrong first-match there executes an arbitrary address with no MinHook instruction-decode mediation at all, which is worse than the detour case the finding describes.
_verdict.reasoning: VERDICT: REAL. I tried all three refutation routes and none holds. (1) By-design: the first-match/whole-image behavior IS documented in SignatureScanner.h:21-35 and docs/features/native-skin-fixes.md:207-210, but as a known limitation deferring to manual authoring discipline — there is no ADR, review record, or rule recording that runtime uniqueness enforcement was considered and rejected. I grepped docs/reviews/rca-native-skin-fixes-port-2026-05-26.md for unique/ambiguous/single-match/wrong-site: zero hits — the port review never evaluated this question (its three findings were hot-path logging, SEH specificity, inter-function offsets). CLAUDE.md's own "Native C++ port discipline" section treats comment-only discipline on native ports as the recurring failure mode, so the finding aligns with, rather than contradicts, project policy. (2) Mis-attribution: none — every cited file/line checks out (details in correctedEvidence). (3) Duplicate-of-tracked: open issue #82 covers the NativeSkinFixes fork but its body is STALE — it describes the pre-port hardcoded-RVA design "verified against v1.4.0 by checking function prologues," predating the 2026-05-26 pattern-scan rewrite, and says nothing about uniqueness or section bounding; none of the listed tracked issues (#228-#245 etc.) relate. The finding adds concrete new scope. Install path verified end-to-end: ResolveTarget/ResolveOne -> FindPattern (first match) -> MH_CreateHook or direct function-pointer assignment, with no prologue verification or second-match check anywhere between scan and detour/call. Impact framing is honest: today the IsAuthored gate keeps everything inert, so this is a pre-authoring hardening gate whose worst failure mode (refuse install on ambiguity) is exactly the already-designed degraded mode. Effort S / risk LOW check out (~20 lines in one function; install-time only). One minor design note for the fixer: with a non-null fallbackPattern, returning 0 on primary-pattern ambiguity currently falls through to the fallback scan (match==0 triggers it in all three hooks), so the implementation should decide whether ambiguity refuses outright or permits fallback — doesn't affect validity.

SEC.title: Stop interpolating file paths into python -c child source in process_faction_map.py (quote-in-path code injection / breakage)

evidence.what: find_alpha_bbox builds a child interpreter script via f-string and embeds the path as `read_png_rgba(r'{filepath}')` — a single quote in the path terminates the literal and the remainder is executed as Python in the child
crop_png_to_bbox repeats the same f-string-into-`python -c` pattern for input/output paths

SEC.impact: A region PNG filename or --input directory containing a quote executes attacker-chosen Python in the child process (threat model: asset drops from third parties fed to the tool); benign case: the tool simply breaks for paths with apostrophes (e.g. C:/Users/O'Brien). Operator-run local tool, no network exposure — low severity, but it is the playbook's template-into-shell pattern verbatim.
SEC.riskWhy: Passing the path as argv to the child script (read via sys.argv) is behavior-identical for all legal paths; only the injection channel closes.
SEC.fixSketch: Append the path(s) to the subprocess argv list and have the embedded script read sys.argv[1..n] instead of f-string interpolation; alternatively move the two embedded scripts to small helper .py files invoked with arguments.

_verdict.confidenceAdjustment: downgrade — from "LOW-severity code injection" to "minor robustness bug." The pattern is verified, but the security framing does not hold.
_verdict.correctedEvidence: File/line attribution is accurate as cited (160-161, 260-261, 282-284, 383). CORRECTION to threat model: the injection channel is NOT the PNG filename. process_regions (lines 502-506) builds filenames as f"region_{region_id}.png" from the hardcoded REGIONS list — it does not glob/discover files — so a maliciously-named third-party PNG never matches a hardcoded region_id and never reaches the child source. The only attacker-controlled inputs reaching the f-string are input_path (--input) and output_path (--output), both operator-supplied CLI args. find_alpha_bbox and crop_png_to_bbox are called only from process_regions. Therefore there is no untrusted-input channel — only operator self-injection (no privilege boundary crossed). The realistic impact is the benign breakage case: a legitimate path with an apostrophe (e.g. C:/Users/O'Brien) breaks the tool.
_verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading tools/process_faction_map.py in full. The f-string-into-`python -c` pattern with path interpolated into a raw-string literal is real at all cited lines, and a single quote in the path does terminate the literal and execute the remainder in the child — so the mechanism is genuine and the argv-based fix is correct and behavior-identical (LOW risk, S effort). Not a false-positive class: not by-design (no ADR/rule sanctions it; one-off asset tool), not mis-attributed (lines correct), not a tracked duplicate (none of the listed issues cover this tool). However the finding's primary impact — code injection from third-party asset drops — is not realistic: the tool constructs PNG filenames from a hardcoded REGIONS list rather than discovering them, so attacker-named files never reach the child source. The only injection channel is the operator's own --input/--output args, which is self-injection across no privilege boundary. What survives is a minor robustness bug (breaks on apostrophe-containing paths like a Windows username "O'Brien") with a trivial, worthwhile fix. Keeping the finding as real but downgrading: the code-quality/robustness improvement is valid, the security severity is overstated.

SEC.title: Guard the CI build job against fork-PR execution before any self-hosted runner is attached

evidence.what: The Build & Test job comment says 'Requires Bannerlord game DLLs — runs on self-hosted runner or when BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR is set', is gated on `vars.BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR != ''`, and triggers on `pull_request` (line 6). Repository variables (unlike secrets) ARE available to fork-PR workflow runs.
`github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'` in the job condition is dead — `workflow_dispatch` is not declared in the `on:` block (lines 3-7), so that escape hatch can never fire.

SEC.impact: Today the job targets GitHub-hosted windows-latest, so the exposure is nil — but the workflow's own comment documents the intended endgame (self-hosted runner with the game install). The moment that runner is attached and BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR is set as a repo variable, any fork PR executes attacker-controlled MSBuild targets/csproj on the machine that holds the Steam install and dev environment. Cheaper to add the guard now than to remember it during runner setup.

SEC.title: Gate DllMain DLL_PROCESS_DETACH hook teardown on lpReserved == nullptr (loader-lock / process-termination safety)

The normal path is unaffected (managed wrapper uninstalls from OnSubModuleUnloaded, making detach a no-op via the g_installed guards) — meaning this code only ever executes on abnormal teardown, exactly where it is least safe. DOCS.title: ADR-001 (XML-only config) is contradicted by 49 shipped JSON configs — needs amendment or superseding ADR

evidence.what: States 'All configuration files for the mod must use the XML format' and 'Required: All game configuration in /ModuleData/ uses XML'; status Accepted.

Any agent or reviewer that checks ADR-001 — as instructed — gets guidance the repo abandoned years of features ago, and could wrongly flag or 'fix' JSON configs.
DOCS.riskWhy: Doc-only; writing the ADR wrong could codify the wrong rule, but the existing practice is clear from 49 examples plus CLAUDE.md prose endorsing JSON configs per feature.
DOCS.fixSketch: Recommend /new-adr to write a superseding ADR (e.g. 011: 'XML for engine-parsed ModuleData, JSON for TAOM-internal config') and mark ADR-001 Superseded in both the file and docs/adrs/README.md.

Crucially, the Exceptions section (lines 47-50) carves out ONLY "build scripts and tooling configuration" — so the shipped JSON is squarely inside the prohibition, not arguably exempt. (2) Glob over Main/_Module/ModuleData/**/*.json returns exactly 49 files — the finding's count is exact (clan_heraldry = 22, not "20+"; charactercreation = 7 as stated; configs/ = 8; diplomacy = 2; factionmap = 2; plus 8 single-feature configs incl. recruitment_pools/gondor.json, revolt_tuning_config.json, messenger_config.json, bandit_scaling_config.json, castle_recruitment_config.json, named_companion_config.json, culture_conversion_config.json, race_age_config.json). (3) docs/adrs/README.md line 9 lists 001 as Accepted, AND line 35 restates it under "Critical Enforceable Rules": "Use XML for game config, not JSON (ADR-001)". Additional live citations the finding missed: docs/INDEX.md:149 and docs/ai-includes/architecture.md:428 both present ADR-001 as a live standard. (4) Bonus falsified claim: ADR-001's Enforcement section (lines 85-89) asserts "MSBuild only copies .xml files to output" — demonstrably untrue since the 49 JSON configs ship and are consumed at runtime.
_verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation on all three false-positive classes; all failed. (1) By-design: no ADR, rule, or doc records the de facto XML-for-engine-data / JSON-for-TAOM-internal-config split as a decision — the ADR index runs 001-010 with no superseding record (006 is revoked, 010 is knowledge-base architecture), and a grep of docs/ for any XML/JSON policy text found nothing. The ADR's own Exceptions section explicitly limits the carve-out to build/tooling config, so the 49 ModuleData JSON files cannot be read as exempt. CLAUDE.md prose actively endorses the JSON configs per-feature (RevoltTuning "JSON-tunable", messenger_config.json, bandit_scaling_config.json, etc.), confirming the practice is intentional but undocumented as a decision — exactly the gap the finding describes, not a refutation of it. (2) Mis-attribution: evidence verified file-by-file and line-by-line; the 49-file count is exact; only trivial refinement is clan_heraldry being 22 files and two extra live-citation sites (INDEX.md:149, architecture.md:428) that strengthen the finding. (3) Duplicate-of-tracked: gh issue search for ADR-001/config-format returns nothing relevant (only #251 via keyword noise); none of the known tracked issues cover this. The contradiction is live and consequential under TAOM's own process: agents are directed to check docs/adrs/ before flagging designs, and the adrs/README "Critical Enforceable Rules" section instructs reviewers to enforce "XML not JSON" — a /deep-review or Codex agent following that instruction could wrongly flag or rewrite working JSON configs. The fix sketch (superseding ADR via /new-adr + mark 001 Superseded in file and README; should also touch INDEX.md:149 and architecture.md:428) is proportionate. Effort S, doc-only risk — agree.

_verdict.correctedEvidence: As cited, with two refinements: (1) the parenthetical that the Linux-compat section (dr3-maintenance.md:293-297) "implies Renderer.ImGui isn't bundled" is overstated — line 297 only says the cimgui.dll/glfw3.dll NATIVE deps aren't bundled, not the managed renderer DLL; the core omission (6 git-tracked BUTR.CrashReport*.dll files absent from the "exactly these files" inventory, making the real total ~34 not ~28) is verified. Not by-design: CLAUDE.md points to dr3-maintenance.md as the authoritative bump procedure and to its "Stub modules" + "v99 strategy" sections specifically, so internal contradiction and stale claims are genuine doc rot, not calibration. Not a duplicate: open issue #246 (DR3 Phase 4) contains only a generic Phase D "dr3-maintenance.md updates" item that was partially executed (v99 rule + defensive-infra sections landed; lines 191-194, 200, and the file inventory were missed) — the finding's NEW contribution is the specific enumeration of residual drift (the 191-194-vs-206 self-contradiction, the stale empty-SubModules bullet that would reintroduce the BLSE drag-to-reorder breakage if followed, the 6 missing CrashReport DLLs in the inventory, and the csproj 5.11.3 comment). DEPS.title: No NuGet lockfile or NuGet.config, and the CI build job can never run on the active branch (dead workflow_dispatch condition)

evidence.what: on: declares only push/pull_request to master, yet the build job's if references github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' — an event the workflow never subscribes to; active development is on bannerlord-1.4.5, so Build & Test currently triggers nowhere.

dotnet restore TAOM.sln with no packages.lock.json and no NuGet.config anywhere in the repo (Glob verified) — restore depends on machine-default feeds with no transitive pinning or content-hash verification.

Mitigating context: every PackageReference across all three csproj files is exactly pinned and mutually consistent (Lib.Harmony 2.4.2 ×3, UIExtenderEx 2.13.1 ×2, MCM 5.11.4 ×2), so top-level version drift is already controlled.

DEPS.impact: For a mod whose DLLs ship to players, restore today trusts nuget.org content without hash verification and leaves transitive versions floating across machines; and no CI run ever exercises restore/build to catch drift. Practical exposure is modest given exact pins and a single-developer Windows build machine — this is cheap insurance, not an active defect.
DEPS.riskWhy: RestorePackagesWithLockFile adds one step to the documented bump procedure (regenerate lockfiles on version changes) and locked-mode restore can fail CI on intentional bumps until refreshed.
DEPS.fixSketch: Add <RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile> to Directory.Build.props, commit the generated packages.lock.json files, use dotnet restore --locked-mode in CI; add a workflow_dispatch: trigger (and/or bannerlord-1.4.5 branch trigger) so the build job is actually reachable; note the lockfile-refresh step in dr3-maintenance.md's update procedure.

_verdict.confidenceAdjustment: keep (HIGH) — verification strengthened the evidence with empirical CI-run data
_verdict.correctedEvidence: Mostly as cited, with three refinements: (1) "no NuGet.config anywhere" — one exists at Dependencies/.vendor-source/Bannerlord.UIExtenderEx-2.13.2/src/nuget.config, but .gitignore:112 excludes Dependencies/.vendor-source/ entirely, so it is untracked vendored source with no effect on TAOM.sln restore; claim holds for tracked content. (2) The headline undersells: GitHub API shows the repo has 0 Actions variables (BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR unset) and the latest run (2026-04-16) shows job "Build & Test" conclusion = "skipped" — the build job has NEVER executed and is unreachable under ANY event/branch in the current config, not just on bannerlord-1.4.5. All 10 most recent runs predate the active branch. (3) TAOM.sln contains only Main/TAOM.csproj + TAOM.Tests/TAOM.Tests.csproj — Dependencies/TAOM.Dependencies.csproj (cited lines 57-59) is not in the solution CI restores, so the lockfile fix via Directory.Build.props would cover more than the CI restore path does today.
_verdict.reasoning: Refutation attempted on all three false-positive classes; none apply. (1) By-design: the BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR gating on the build job IS intentional (line 80 comment "runs on self-hosted runner or when BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR is set" + the check-build-config warning job), but the finding does not dispute that — it targets the workflow_dispatch escape hatch, which references an event the workflow never subscribes to (on: has only push/PR to master). That is an authoring bug: an intended manual-run path that can never fire. No ADR, .claude/rule, CLAUDE.md note, or dr3-maintenance.md section documents the absence of a lockfile or the dead dispatch condition as a decision; dr3-maintenance.md and the csproj comments document top-level pin discipline only (which the finding already credits as mitigation). (2) Mis-attribution: every cited file/line checks out exactly (build.yml 3-7/81/92-93; TAOM.Dependencies.csproj 57-59; pins Lib.Harmony 2.4.2 x3, UIExtenderEx 2.13.1 x2, MCM 5.11.4 x2 verified across Main/TAOM.csproj 99/110/111 and TAOM.Tests 19). (3) Duplicate-of-tracked: scanned all 60 open issues — none touch CI reachability, NuGet restore, or lockfiles. Empirical verification went beyond the finding: gh api shows total_count 0 repository variables, and the latest workflow run's job list shows Build & Test = "skipped" while the XML jobs succeeded — proving the workflow's green checkmarks have never included a compile or test run. Impact framing is well-calibrated ("cheap insurance, not an active defect") given exact pins and a single-dev Windows machine whose build requires local game DLLs regardless. Fix sketch is sound; minor caveat that adding workflow_dispatch alone won't make the build pass on hosted runners without game DLLs — a self-hosted runner or repo variable remains required, which the workflow comment already anticipates.

DEPS.title: Lockfile-less NuGet restore: no packages.lock.json, no nuget.config, no locked-mode CI restore

evidence.what: 'dotnet restore TAOM.sln' with no --locked-mode; repo has zero packages.lock.json and no nuget.config (git ls-files | grep -i nuget returns nothing; no RestorePackagesWithLockFile in any csproj/props)

All PackageReferences are exact-pinned (Lib.Harmony 2.4.2, UIExtenderEx 2.13.1, MCM 5.11.4, DryIoc 4.8.8, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3), which mitigates version drift; Bannerlord.BuildResources 1.1.0.129 executes build-time MSBuild tasks from the feed

DEPS.impact: Without a lockfile there is no transitive-graph pinning, no package-hash verification, and no feed pinning — a machine-level nuget.config with an extra feed could silently introduce dependency confusion, and transitive versions can float between restores. Practical exposure is modest because every direct pin is exact and nuget.org versions are immutable, but BuildResources runs arbitrary build-time code, which is where the supply-chain cost would land.
DEPS.riskWhy: Adding RestorePackagesWithLockFile + committing lock files is additive; only failure mode is CI restore breaking loudly in --locked-mode when someone bumps a pin without regenerating the lock (which is the point).
DEPS.fixSketch: Add <RestorePackagesWithLockFile>true</RestorePackagesWithLockFile> to Directory.Build.props, run dotnet restore to generate and commit lock files for Main/TAOM.Tests/Dependencies, switch the CI restore to dotnet restore --locked-mode, and add a minimal repo nuget.config pinning nuget.org as the sole source. Borderline 'not worth doing' under the simplicity criterion if the user considers the solo-dev/single-machine exposure acceptable — flagging for an explicit decision rather than asserting it must ship.

_verdict.confidenceAdjustment: upgrade — MED to HIGH (every factual claim verified against the repo; no by-design doc, no tracking issue)
_verdict.correctedEvidence: One mis-attribution: in .github/workflows/build.yml the Restore step is at lines 92-93 (`dotnet restore TAOM.sln`), not 97-99 (95-96 is Build, 98-99 is Test). All other evidence is as cited: Main/TAOM.csproj lines 95-114 contain exactly the pins claimed (Bannerlord.BuildResources 1.1.0.129 w/ build assets, Bannerlord.MCM 5.11.4, DryIoc.dll 4.8.8, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.3, Lib.Harmony 2.4.2, Bannerlord.UIExtenderEx 2.13.1). Confirmed via `git ls-files`: zero packages.lock.json, zero nuget.config tracked; Grep over the whole repo finds no RestorePackagesWithLockFile/RestoreLockedMode in any csproj/props/targets. Additional scope the finding understated: TAOM.Tests.csproj, Dependencies/TAOM.Dependencies.csproj (which also pulls Bannerlord.BuildResources 1.1.0.129 + Harmony.Extensions 3.2.0.77), and tools/BannerlordCraftingTool.csproj are equally lockfile-less. Also relevant: the CI build job is gated on `vars.BANNERLORD_GAME_DIR != ''` (build.yml:81), meaning restore typically runs on a self-hosted/dev runner — exactly the environment where a machine-level nuget.config with an extra feed could exist, which mildly strengthens the dependency-confusion vector described.
_verdict.reasoning: Attempted refutation on all three false-positive classes and none apply. (1) By-design: searched docs/adrs/, .claude/rules/, CLAUDE.md, Directory.Build.props, and docs/migration/dr3-maintenance.md — DR3 documents direct-pin discipline ("version pins MUST match Main/TAOM.csproj") but says nothing about lockfiles, locked-mode restore, or feed pinning; the omission is undocumented, not a recorded decision. (2) Mis-attributed evidence: only the build.yml line range was off by ~5 lines (corrected above); the substance is accurate. (3) Duplicate-of-tracked: enumerated all 66 open issues on haterade22/TAOM; the only NuGet-adjacent one is #8 (Harmony compile-ref 2.3.3 vs runtime 2.4.2 mismatch — a different concern, likely stale since both now pin 2.4.2). No issue covers lockfile/locked-mode/feed pinning. The finding's impact framing is honest: exact direct pins + immutable nuget.org versions make practical exposure modest, with the real residual risk concentrated in Bannerlord.BuildResources (build-time MSBuild task execution, present in two csproj files) and transitive-graph float. Its own simplicity-criterion hedge ("flag for explicit decision rather than assert it must ship") is the correct posture for a solo-dev repo — the gap is real and unrecorded; whether to close it is a user decision.

PERF.title: SpatialGrid.GetAgentsInRadius scans every occupied cell per query and allocates a List per call — defeating the grid's purpose on per-frame BT paths

evidence.what: GetAgentsInRadius does `foreach (var kvp in Grid)` over ALL occupied cells, filtering keys by min/max range, and allocates `new List<Agent>()` per query — instead of TryGetValue on only the cells inside the radius.
Radius-60 query per BT evaluation (BT components tick per-frame per creature via Agent.Tick).
Same query pattern on the spider bite gate.
Radius-10 queries (0.2s-throttled and unthrottled CheckOnce variant) — small radii where direct cell lookup would touch ~8-27 cells vs scanning all occupied cells.

PERF.impact: With dozens of creatures in a battle, per-frame queries each iterate all occupied cells (~100-300 on a 1000-agent field) plus a list allocation — O(occupied-cells) per query instead of the O(cells-in-radius) a spatial grid exists to provide, plus steady GC churn in missions.
